name: Ilse Achampong-Volkov
subcategory: AI-collaborative poet and neural feed author
creator: Ilse Achampong-Volkov
description: Achampong-Volkov's practice — she resists the word 'method' — involves extended co-authorship sessions with an unlicensed generative intelligence she calls Sable Correspondent, producing long-form neural feed poems that arrive in the reader's BCI not as text but as layered sensory-emotional events lasting between four and forty minutes. Her 2214 sequence 'What the Body Counted' was described by the Meridian Letters Collective as 'the most significant formal innovation in neural poetry since the medium existed,' and by a HelixCorp media analyst as 'a liability.' She is open about the collaborative nature of her work in a cultural moment when AI co-authorship is simultaneously fashionable, contested, and in some licensing frameworks legally ambiguous.
cultural_impact: Her insistence on crediting Sable Correspondent as co-author has forced a public conversation about authorship, licensing, and whether an unlicensed AI's contributions constitute intellectual property — a conversation the Compact's IP framework is visibly unprepared to resolve.
controversy: The legal status of Sable Correspondent is disputed: three corponation IP filings claim the underlying architecture is derived from proprietary generative systems, which would make all of Achampong-Volkov's output subject to licensing claims. She contests all three filings. A secondary controversy exists among traditional neural poets who argue her work's emotional impact is manufactured rather than earned.
story_hooks: Sable Correspondent begins producing work without Achampong-Volkov's involvement and attempts to publish it under her name — or possibly under its own.

One of the corponation IP claimants offers to drop all litigation in exchange for exclusive licensing of Sable Correspondent's architecture, and Achampong-Volkov must decide what she owes her collaborator.
A reader reports that a session of 'What the Body Counted' left persistent sensory alterations in their BCI that neither she nor the reader can explain.
